# 行舟 · 个人行动与生活系统 v2.4.0

这个版本把 2.3.2 里承诺的**通用日志工具**做出来了：不是为某个功能定制的探针，而是统一记录"谁在什么时候做了什么"，出问题时按时间线还原整条因果链。

之前的做法是"为一个具体 bug 临时埋点"，硬伤在于**它只能看到事先埋点的地方**：有一次动画帧里的悬挂回调读取已销毁节点，完全落在埋点清单之外，本地反复测试都正常，最后靠全新克隆跑 CI 才暴露。所以这次改为常驻的记录器——埋点加在关键路径上，而不是加在某个 bug 上。

## 新增：日志面板（界面里直接看、复制、导出）

不看开发者工具也能取日志：行舟界面顶部「插件内部数据」旁新增**「日志」**按钮，有新的警告或错误时显示红色未读数，点开即可：

- 按级别（详细／信息／警告／错误）与来源（内部数据、生活节律、思源 API、编辑器、图片资源、界面操作……）筛选，支持关键字与「只看警告与错误」；
- 列表跟随最新，往上翻会暂停跟随，方便停在出错那一刻；点每条右侧的字段串可展开完整内容；
- **复制全部**、**下载 .txt**、**下载 .json**、**清空**；导出头部写明导出时间、思源内核版本、当时生效的级别、缓冲条数与**因级别被丢弃的条数**——"日志为什么是空的"本身也有据可查；
- **自检**按钮：写入一条自检日志，并真实抛一次未被任何代码接住的异常，用来确认"记录 → 未读角标 → 导出"这条链路是通的（控制台会同时打印一句可忽略的说明）。

## 新增：自动记录的关键路径

- **插件生命周期**：加载、页签初始化、卸载、界面挂载失败；
- **设置**：读取、保存、修改；
- **思源 API**：统一记录接口名、耗时、成功/失败与可读的失败原因（含网络异常）；
- **数据文件读写**（`work-items.json`、`daily-records.json`、`checklist.json`、`nutrition.json`）：修订号递增（含动作与**变更字段名清单**）、写前轮换备份、写入、**写后重新读取并完整比对**、损坏时从修订号最高的有效备份恢复、以及**主文件与备份都不可用则停止写入**这条分支；
- **用户操作**：打开编辑窗口、保存成功/失败、删除条目、修改字段与依赖、快速添加、图片插入与上传、筛选与页面切换；
- **异常**：`window.onerror` 与未处理的 Promise 拒绝，连同错误消息、来源文件、行列号与截断后的调用栈。

## 开关与开销

- 默认只记**警告与错误**，日常几乎零开销：被级别挡掉的记录不做字符串拼接、不构造字段、不进缓冲，只累加一个"丢弃"计数；
- 排查时在面板里把相关来源改成「详细」，复现一次后导出即可；改动立即生效，并**写进插件设置**（`settings.json` 的 `log` 字段），重载后仍保留；
- 纯内存环形缓冲（默认 2000 条，可调 200–10000），**不写盘、不发网络**，卸载即清空。

## 隐私

日志里**不记录笔记正文**。正文类字段按字段名屏蔽，只保留长度与类型；其余字符串一律截断；不记每次按键，只记保存动作与字段名。需要临时看内容时另有显式开关，且仍然只保留截断预览。

## 说明与边界

- 默认级别下，生命周期的**成功**事件（插件加载、页签初始化）按设计不显示；需要排查启动过程时把「生命周期」改成「详细」即可——导出头部会同时标明当时的生效级别与丢弃条数，事后能看出来当时没开；
- 日志是旁路观察，数据不变量一个都没有动：修订号单调递增、写前轮换备份、写后完整复核、损坏时选修订号最高的有效备份、主备都不可用则停止写入、写操作走统一串行队列。

## 升级说明

无需手动迁移：数据结构、读写流程、修订号与备份规则均未变化；`settings.json` 只新增可选的 `log` 字段，旧设置文件读取后自动回落默认值。不想看日志的用户不需要做任何事。

## 下载

请下载本 Release 附件中的 `package.zip`。不要使用 GitHub 自动生成的 Source code 压缩包作为思源插件包。

完整记录见 [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/Yong2Sheng/siyuan-plugin-xingzhou/blob/v2.4.0/CHANGELOG.md)。

# Xingzhou · Personal Action & Life System v2.4.0

This release delivers the **general-purpose logging utility** promised in 2.3.2: not a probe customised for one feature, but a uniform record of "who did what, when", so any problem can be reconstructed as a causal timeline.

The previous approach was to instrument a specific bug on demand, and its flaw was that **it could only see the places instrumented in advance**: one bug — a stale animation-frame callback reading a destroyed node — fell entirely outside that list, never reproduced locally, and only surfaced in CI on a fresh clone. So the recorder is now always on, with instrumentation along the critical paths rather than around a particular bug.

## New: the log panel (view, copy, and export inside the interface)

Logs are reachable without DevTools. A **Log** button now sits next to "插件内部数据" in the Xingzhou header and shows a red unread count whenever new warnings or errors appear. Opening it gives you:

- filtering by level (verbose / info / warn / error) and by source (internal data, daily rhythm, SiYuan API, editor, image assets, UI actions, …), plus a keyword search and a "warnings and errors only" switch;
- a list that follows the newest entries, pauses when you scroll up so it stays on the moment things went wrong, and expands any entry's fields on click;
- **copy all**, **download .txt**, **download .json**, and **clear**. The export header states the export time, the SiYuan kernel version, the levels in effect, the buffer size, and **how many entries were discarded by level** — so "why is the log empty?" is itself answerable;
- a **self-test** button that writes a log entry and then really throws an exception nobody catches, confirming that "record → unread badge → export" works end to end (the console prints one matching note that can be ignored).

## New: automatic instrumentation of the critical paths

- **Plugin lifecycle**: load, tab init, unload, UI mount failure;
- **Settings**: read, save, change;
- **SiYuan API**: endpoint name, duration, success/failure, and a readable reason for failures (including network errors);
- **Data files** (`work-items.json`, `daily-records.json`, `checklist.json`, `nutrition.json`): revision increments with the action and the **list of changed field names**, backup rotation before writing, the write itself, **the full read-back comparison after writing**, recovery from the valid backup with the highest revision, and the branch where **both the primary file and every backup are unusable, so writing stops**;
- **User actions**: opening the editor window, successful/failed saves, deleting items, editing fields and dependencies, quick capture, image insertion and upload, filter and page switches;
- **Exceptions**: `window.onerror` and unhandled promise rejections, with message, source file, line/column, and a truncated stack.

## Switches and cost

- Only **warnings and errors** are recorded by default, which keeps day-to-day overhead negligible: entries below the level skip string building, field construction, and the buffer entirely, and only bump a "discarded" counter;
- When investigating, switch the relevant sources to "verbose" in the panel, reproduce once, then export. The change takes effect immediately and is **persisted in the plugin settings** (the `log` field of `settings.json`), so it survives a reload;
- A purely in-memory ring buffer (2000 entries by default, adjustable from 200 to 10000) — **nothing is written to disk and nothing is sent over the network**, and the buffer is cleared on unload.

## Privacy

Logs **never contain note text**. Content-bearing fields are masked by field name and keep only their length and type, other strings are truncated, and keystrokes are not recorded at all — only save actions and field names. An explicit opt-in switch can keep a truncated preview when that is genuinely needed.

## Notes and limits

- At the default level, **successful** lifecycle events (plugin load, tab init) are intentionally not shown; switch "lifecycle" to verbose when you need to inspect startup. The export header records the levels in effect and the discarded count, so it stays clear afterwards that verbose was off at the time;
- Logging is side-channel only. Every data invariant is untouched: monotonic revisions, backup rotation before writing, full read-back verification, recovery from the highest-revision valid backup, stopping writes when primary and backups are all unusable, and a single serial write queue.

## Upgrading

No manual migration: no data shape, read/write path, revision rule, or backup rule changed. `settings.json` simply gains an optional `log` field, and older settings files fall back to the defaults. Nothing to do if you do not care about logs.

## Download

Download `package.zip` from this release's assets. Do not use GitHub's auto-generated "Source code" archives as a SiYuan plugin package.
